recommendation: Keep the audit commit unless someone with Jira attachment access can recover Archive.zip. If recovered, compare its CDS QA entries against current build-scoped CDS/Clinical Reasoning source and make precise follow-up fixes only for remaining substantive discrepancies.
issue_request: FHIR-17599 asked editors to use the attached Archive.zip QA review files from an earlier QA process to check that updates had been applied. Jira records status Published, resolution Persuasive/Auto-approved, applied-for version STU3, related page FHIR-core-many, and a comment from Bryn Rhodes saying the updates were verified as applied.
initial_application: No source reference, commit message, or history search result explicitly mentions FHIR-17599, GF#17599, or #17599. Historical CDS/Clinical Reasoning QA work exists in March 2018 GuidanceResponse, Library, Measure, and MeasureReport QA commits; a September 2018 CDS Resources QA commit; and November 2018 Clinical Reasoning module review commits, but none can be tied to attachment 15595 or to this Jira key.
additional_context: Attachment 15595 could not be downloaded in this environment: both the secure attachment URL and the REST attachment-content URL returned HTTP 403. source/fhir.ini lists active CDS-owned resources and pages, and tracked qa/*.docx review documents exist, but no active build reference to the QA archive or a current source index of its entries was found. Jira search found sibling QA reports issues for other work groups, and Zulip/Confluence searches found no direct FHIR-17599 clarification.
reconciliation: Published an empty human-review audit commit. No source file was changed because the only detailed requested changes are inside an inaccessible attachment and there is no verifiable current-source defect to fix without speculating.
